title: Distributed Tables missing records. "Exception: Too large string size." in logs.
body:
Setup:
```
         <shard>
              <weight>1</weight>
              <internal_replication>false</internal_replication>
              <replica>
                  <host><server1domainname></host>
                  <port>9000</port>
              </replica>
              <replica>
                  <host><server2domainname></host>
                  <port>9000</port>
              </replica>
          </shard>

```
Our code writes to a Distributed table on either server, and then clickhouse writes the record to the underlying real tables on both servers. 

No zookeeper.

This has been working for a few years.

Incident.
To get multivolume support, I upgraded from 18.14.19 to 20.8.12.2. I had a number of problems, and ran out of time to debug/fix, so I rolled back to 18.14.19. My problem probably started then.

Now we have discovered that some records are not getting replicated to one of the servers. Or maybe replication is working from server1 -> server2, but not the other way. I'm not 100% sure. When reads randomly choose a server, they get different results.

I have these error messages constantly on one server:

`2021.03.19 02:35:13.294443 [ 39 ] {} <Error> <table>.Distributed.DirectoryMonitor: Poco::Exception. Code: 1000, e.code() = 0, e.displayText() = Exception: Too large string size., e.what() = Exception
`

I also noticed a small number of these errors on the other server, but they are not constant. Only a handful from a few hours ago.

`2021.03.18 19:22:36.647630 [ 38 ] {} <Error> <table>.Distributed.DirectoryMonitor: Code: 252, e.displayText() = DB::Exception: Received from <serverdomainname>:9000, <ipaddress> DB::Exception: Too many parts (304). Merges are processing significantly slower than inserts..
`

I did some research into the first error, but I don't really understand which directory, or which string it is referring to.

Thanks.
author: entropical

comments.body:
You don't have actual Replication. 
Distributed table propagates inserts into 2 CH nodes. Sometimes inserts can fail into one replica and succeed into another.
There is no surprise that Replicas has different data. It's documented behavior for this setup.

 >Poco::Exception. Code: 1000, e.code() = 0, e.displayText() = Exception: Too large string size

You should stop insertion and check what is going in Distributed table catalog. 
Probably drop Distributed table. Remove all remains of Distributed folder (/var/lib/clickhouse/data/db/distributedtablename/) and create Distributed table back.

> Too many parts (304). Merges are

Need to check what is going on with `<serverdomainname>:9000` in this server logs. And in `select * from system.merges`

>I did some research into the first error, but I don't really understand which directory, or which string it is referring to.

It's about `/var/lib/clickhouse/data/db/distributedtablename/.....`

> You don't have actual Replication.
> It's documented behavior for this setup.

Yeah, I did know this, but up until very recently it has been sufficient for our purpose.

> It's about /var/lib/clickhouse/data/db/distributedtablename/.....

Right! I noticed this directory when I had the failed upgrade.

I have two directories here, but I think I should only have one. One has IP, one has domainname. I'm pretty sure this is related to the version change.

/var/lib/clickhouse/data/noc/distributedtablename/
default@111%2E222%2E333%2E444:9000/
default@domainname%2Etld%2Etld%2Etld%2Ecom:9000/

> Probably drop Distributed table. Remove all remains of Distributed folder (/var/lib/clickhouse/data/db/distributedtablename/) and create Distributed table back.

Yeah, this sounds like it might help. This is safe, right, because the Distributed table doesn't actually contain data? Trying not to lose any (more...) data.

>This is safe, right, because the Distributed table doesn't actually contain data? 

Yes. It is safe. It contains only not propagated inserts. That's why I suggest to stop insertion.
Check that it stops to propagate. 
Check the size of these subdirectories: `du -sh /var/lib/clickhouse/data/noc/distributedtablename/*`
If it's huge, check how many .bin files inside. Check the server logs.

On one server, both of these directories are very small.
On the other server, the one with the IP address in as the name is small. The one with the domain name appears to be so huge I can't even ls or du it.

> Remove all remains of Distributed folder

Hypothetically, if there are orphaned bin files here, can I reintroduce them after I recreate the Distributed table, and it is working? I'm not _too_ concerned if not, just working out my options.

Thanks for your excellent help by the way.

>Hypothetically, if there are orphaned bin files here, 
>can I reintroduce them after I recreate the Distributed table, and it is working?
> I'm not too concerned if not, just working out my options.

If you sure that both directories are the same destination you can move files from the one to anther.
And yes, you can move files / rename (move) the whole  directory to somewhere to /var/lib/clickhouse
recreate the distr. table and move .bin files one by one or  1000 by 1000 ( batches ).
I stopped my writers, and am now dropping the replicatedtable. It has taken about 10 minutes so far...

The drop was taking forever. I think it was attempting to catch up on the pending propogations first.

I moved the directory to a safe location, and the drop completed a few seconds later. I then recreated the distributed table, and started my writers. For the last hour it looks like the propagations are working fine.

I'll now try to reparent my orphan bin files.

Thanks again for your help @den-crane.

title: Connecttion refused after kill the clickhouse server process
body:
I have a clickhouse table containing more than 40 billion records.  One day I want to modify a parameter in my config.xml. So I attempted to stop the server but it was stuck. I guess there were many background processes working. Then I kill the clickhouse server with "kill -9".
However when I tried to restart the server and run clickhouse-client again, I got "connection refused". 
If I remove all data partitions and the corresponding table metadata (sql), it works fine again. Once I move the table data back to its position, I got the same error "connection refused" again.

**How to reproduce**
if I tried to stop the clickhosue server process with "kill -9", but not "clickhouse-server stop". the error occurs. Especially when its a massive table.

* Which ClickHouse server version to use
version 20.0.10

If any ideas? Thanks.
author: y45398jp123

comments.body:
40 billion records -- it's not big table. There are installation with 40 trillions.
CH start time depends on number of parts (table partitioning).

Can you show 
`select count() from system.parts`?
`select count() from system.columns where tables = ....` ?

Thanks for your reply @den-crane 
the table contains 14521 partitions and 119 columns.
do i have to wait for longer time after restart the server before trying to connect? have no idea...
Thanks.

>The table contains 14521 partitions and 119 columns.

Then slow start is expected. Especially on slow HDD or IOPS limited cloud disks (like AWS EBS GP1)
You should wait longer  for a start minutes. I've heard that in case of 100000 CH can start up to 40 minutes.
This is expected by design. Because CH reads reads every part (metadata) on start. 

You can use disks with low latency (SSD/NVME) or reduce number of partitions (by re-desingning your table -- partition by section).
thanks so much for reply, quick and professional !

satisfaction_conditions: An explanation for why the server connection is refused after a forced kill
Information about expected server behavior with large datasets
Guidance on appropriate wait times for server restart
Technical explanation of why the server takes time to start
Practical recommendations to improve the situation

title: No data in replicated table
body:
I have two replicas. Data are inserted into table in replica A. Table counterpart in replica B is empty though. Data are not replicated between replicas. I tried recreating table in replica B but it did not trigger the sync.

Replication for other tables is working just fine.

What can I do to debug the issue? `show create table` gives same result for both replicas.

ClickHouse version 20.6
author: simPod

comments.body:
check (at both nodes) : select * from system.replication_queue 

wrong ZK path? different shards?

I don't have multiple shards.

replication queue does not contain any records for the target table

path is the same (reported by show create table)

🤔
Show `grep tablename clickhouseserver.log`
I tried grepping `cat /var/log/clickhouse-server/clickhouse-server.log` in both replicas but for this particular table contains no logs (it does have some warnings for larger tables though).

It could be anything. How did you copy/pasted / attached zk path when you created a table?

For example these two strings are different. 
Latin:    /ccccc/ 
Сyrrylic: /ссссс/ 

Check zookeeper select * from system.zookeeper where path = '/..zk_path/replicas
Check select * from system.replicas where table = ...

> select * from system.zookeeper where path = '/..zk_path/replicas
Gives result on both replicas. 

But on the B, there's `replicas	last added replica: A` (version: 1)
For fully replicated tables it's `replicas	last added replica: B` (version: 4)

`system.replicas` says the `total_replicas` is 1. Seems like those tables are disconnected on both replicas. Is there a way to get in in sync somehow?

> How did you copy/pasted / attached zk path when you created a table?

I did it a long time ago but It was simple CREATE TABLE ON CLUSTER I believe

Check at both servers that zhash is identical 
```

select replica_name, total_replicas, active_replicas, zookeeper_path, 
           cityHash64(zookeeper_path) zhash, hex(zookeeper_path) 
from system.replicas
where table = '....'
```
Zookeeper paths differ in a small typo :/ Thank you very much for helping me debug this. I have setup a new monitoring query to catch this in the future.

title: Log file not recreated if deleted
body:
Hi,

My ClickHouse is integrated with a system that regularly take the log files, backup them, and delete them locally. It is a common system to lots of services.

Nevertheless, I got an issue with clickhouse. If you delete one ClickHouse log file when ClickHouse is up and running, the log file will not be recreated, and all new clickhouse logs will be lost.

Forcing the reload of the config file or flushing the log  (SYSTEM RELOAD CONFIG or SYSTEM FLUSH LOGS) does not seems to fix the issue.

So is there a way to force clickhouse to recreate the log file ?
author: edonin

comments.body: You can send SIGHUP to clickhouse-server to create next log file.

Super, it is working.

Thanks

satisfaction_conditions: A method to force ClickHouse to recreate log files after they've been deleted
A solution that works with ClickHouse's running state without requiring restart
A solution compatible with external log management systems
